newsitem.title: USA: FSA sees no First Merchants loss.
newsitem.headline: FSA sees no First Merchants loss.

text.p: Financial Security Assurance said Tuesday it does not expect to incur any losses on $503 million of auto loan transactions it insured that were sponsored by First Merchants Acceptance Corp.
First Merchants said Tuesday it is in default under its secured senior loan agreement with its banks, and may seek protection under the United States Bankruptcy Code.

"We have been monitoring the First Merchants situation very carefully for some time and do not expect to experience any losses on any of our eight insured auto loan transactions, which are backed by subprime loans," Russell Brewer, managing director and chief underwriting officer at FSA, said in a statement.
FSA has a total outstanding net par exposure to First Merchants of $503 million, with an expected remaining average life on the deals of about 1.5 years, according to the statement.
Brewer said the FSA-insured issues are "substantially over-collateralized and the assets supporting them are held in bankruptcy remote special purpose vehicles."
He said FSA has taken action to ensure that effective servicing on the portfolios continues.
